_readme: Hand-labelled regression set for the evidence pipeline (engine v4).
NOT EXPERT-LABELLED. One labeller (the engineer fixing the pipeline), reading each study's stored PICO, outcome string and verbatim quote; no second reviewer, no adjudication, no clinical expertise.
It is a regression net for known failure modes (wrong population, wrong exposure, mis-signed direction, off-outcome matches, mixed outcome tiers), not a benchmark of correctness.

Fields: in_scope = the study legitimately answers the topic question (right exposure, right population, an asked outcome). tier = 1 clinical event/primary outcome, 2 validated surrogate or anthropometric, 3 other biomarker. stance = relative to what the question asks (favorable supports it, unfavorable contradicts it, null no significant effect, unclear no direction). confidence 'uncertain' labels are recorded but not asserted by the test. known_miss = a place where the pipeline is still wrong; the test expects it to fail (xfail, non-strict).

The set was chosen from the studies behind the contested verdicts (sat-fat, sglt2-hf, vitd, fasting, ssb, red-meat, fiber, plant-based, fruit-veg, low-carb, sweeteners, coffee), so it over-represents suspicious studies and says nothing about the false-negative rate.

labels.why: Meta-analysis of SFA-reduction trials; all-cause mortality RR 0.96 (0.88-1.06): no significant effect.
LDL falls with a HIGHER P:S ratio, i.e. with LESS saturated fat: supports 'SFA raises LDL'. (Was mis-signed as contradicting.)
Outcome is inflammatory bowel disease onset; 'cholesterol' is only the exposure descriptor.
Outcome is gestational diabetes in pregnancy.
LDL cholesterol; the extracted result is a correlation across all diets with no arm direction.
Cerebrovascular mortality, dietary cholesterol quintiles: HR 0.48 (0.18-1.23), not significant.
Men with non-metastatic prostate cancer; mortality is post-diagnosis prognosis, not the effect in general adults.
Butter (an SFA source) highest vs lowest: total mortality HR 1.15 (1.08-1.22).
CAD mortality per 300 mg/d dietary cholesterol HR 1.42 (1.09-1.86).
Stroke survivors: mortality after the index event, not a general adult population.
Myocardial infarction per 100 mg/d dietary cholesterol RR 1.05 (1.02-1.08). A valid CV outcome even though the word 'cardiovascular' is absent.
Waist circumference / metabolic syndrome: not one of the outcomes asked about (CV risk, LDL, mortality).
Olive oil vs BUTTER: the exposure (butter) is the COMPARATOR arm; total cholesterol rose with butter -> supports. (Was mis-signed as contradicting.)
Ovarian cancer patients, survival after diagnosis.
Mediterranean diet adherence and lung-cancer-specific mortality: neither the exposure (fat) nor the outcome (CV) of the question.
Replacing SFA with unsaturated fat; CVD incidence lower with a better lipidome score. Indirect (lipid score) exposure.
Primary composite (CV death or worsening HF) HR 0.86 (0.68-1.08), P=0.20: null in the trial itself.
HHF HR 0.68 with dapagliflozin vs placebo; population is T2D with CV risk (not established HF).
Only result is how HF stage predicts events in the PLACEBO group: prognostic, not a treatment effect.
Canagliflozin vs placebo reduced HF/CV death in the low-normal-sodium stratum; overall effect not separately extracted.
labels.known_miss: The counted finding is a sodium-intake stratum, not the overall effect.

labels.why: Only atrial-fibrillation and sinus-rhythm strata are extracted; no overall effect.
labels.known_miss: The AF stratum is counted as the headline (no sibling-stratum detection).

labels.why: Fractures, 1600 IU/day arm vs placebo HR 1.52 (1.06-2.18); the 3200 IU arm was null. A single dose arm is what is extracted.
labels.known_miss: Arm selection: only the 1600 IU arm is extracted.

Pools unsweetened and sugar-sweetened tea; sugar-sweetened tea alone is not isolated.
